name: Advocates for Children of New York
recommendations_evidence: "City Budget Priorities for Fiscal Year 2027" (January 22, 2026) and "AFC Testifies on the New York City FY 2027 Preliminary Budget - Children and Youth" (March 16, 2026), both on the policy-resources listing.

volume_2025_plus.note: X-WP-Total: 61 from https://advocatesforchildren.org/wp-json/wp/v2/policy-resource?after=2025-01-01T00:00:00 (the policy-resource custom post type holds reports, testimony, budget responses and coalition letters; 492 items total). A separate 'resource' custom post type returned X-WP-Total: 22 for the same window, but those are parent- and educator-facing know-your-rights guides rather than policy documents, so they are excluded from this count.

verdict_reason: Highest-volume producer in this group of dated New York City Council testimony, budget-priority documents and policy reports with explicit asks of city government.
notes: The /feed/ is a decoy - 2,125 bytes and the wp/v2/posts collection holds stale legacy content. All current output sits in custom post types exposed at wp-json/wp/v2/types: policy-resource (492), resource, article, litigation, story, event, person, topic. Use per_page=100 with the 'after' parameter; REST caps at 100 per page so the full policy-resource archive is 5 pages. Titles come back HTML-entity-encoded (& for ampersands) and need unescaping. AFC also runs a litigation practice (separate 'litigation' post type), but that is in addition to, not instead of, its policy publishing.

name: Citizens' Committee for Children of New York
recommendations_evidence: "New York City FY 2027 Budget Priorities" (April 9, 2026) instructs the city to "Increase funding for NYC Care from $100 million to $200 million."

volume_2025_plus.note: X-WP-Total: 83 from https://cccnewyork.org/wp-json/wp/v2/data_publications?after=2025-01-01T00:00:00 (738 items total in the type). Spot-checked against the first REST page, whose visible dates run 2026-07-09 back to 2026-02-17 in the top 25, consistent with roughly weekly output.

verdict_reason: Publishes budget-priority documents, City Council testimony and the annual Keeping Track of New York City's Children with explicit dollar-figure asks of city government.
notes: Gotcha: https://cccnewyork.org/publications/ is NOT a listing - it is an Algolia-powered search UI that renders zero items until a query is typed. Confirmed in a real browser (page text shows only 'Search CCC's Archive of Publications / Refine Your Search'), so this is a JS-rendered dead end, not a curl blocking problem. /data-publications/ 404s and ?post_type=data_publications returns HTTP 500; there is no wp-sitemap for the type. The reliable listing is the wp-json data_publications collection (25 pages at per_page=30, capped at 100 per page). Item permalinks are under /data-publications/<slug>/. Titles are HTML-entity-encoded. Recent output is roughly half New York City and half New York State budget advocacy. Annual flagship confirmed on the feed: 'Keeping Track of New York City's Children | 2026' (May 14, 2026).

name: Coalition for the Homeless
recommendations_evidence: "State of the Homeless 2026: A Crisis Inherited, A Choice Ahead" (June 2026) tells Mayor Mamdani to "Commit to build and provide sufficient capital funding for at least 12,000 new units of deeply-subsidized affordable housing for homeless and ELI households every year for the next five years."

volume_2025_plus.note: 13 unique dated testimony PDFs with 2025-01 or later upload paths counted on the testimony listing page (2025-01 through 2026-03), plus 2 annual flagship reports counted on the State of the Homeless archive page (State of the Homeless 2025: Nowhere to Go, June 2025; State of the Homeless 2026: A Crisis Inherited, A Choice Ahead, June 2026). The separate Research Reports and Policy Briefs page has nothing newer than May 2022, so it contributes 0.

verdict_reason: Publishes an annual flagship report and a steady stream of New York City Council budget and oversight testimony containing explicit, itemized demands on the mayor and city agencies.
notes: Reports and testimony live on static HTML pages that link directly to PDFs; dates are inferred from the /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/ path plus the on-page listing. No pagination on the testimony page (139 unique PDFs on one page). Three separate listing pages: /advocacy-library/research-and-policy/testimony/ (testimony, current through 2026-03), /advocacy-library/research-and-policy/state-of-the-homeless-archive/ (22 annual reports back to 2004), and /advocacy-library/research-and-policy/research-reports-policy-briefs/ (53 PDFs, stale since 2022). The /advocacy-library/ hub is a filterable search UI that shows only six 'recommended' documents by default. wp-json/wp/v2/types exposes no custom post types, but wp-json/wp/v2/search returns subtypes 'advocacy-files' and 'press' that have no REST collection endpoint (404). /feed/ carries news and blog posts, not reports.

name: Community Service Society of New York
recommendations_evidence: Testimony: Ensure Fair, Transparent Co-op Access for All New Yorkers (December 2nd, 2025) - "Ensuring fair access to co-ops gives more working- and middle-class New Yorkers a meaningful chance to build wealth and stability. CSS strongly urges the NYC Council to pass Intro 407."

volume_2025_plus.note: 46 dated items on /publications (pages P0-P64, meta line 'Policy Brief | Jun. 2026' etc.) with a 2025 or 2026 date, plus 28 dated testimony items on /news/c/testimony (20 on page 1 back to March 18, 2025, plus 8 more on /news/c/testimony/P20 back to January 30, 2025). Item types include Report, Policy Brief, Survey and Annual Report.

verdict_reason: High-volume publisher of dated policy briefs, survey reports and New York City Council testimony that make explicit asks of city government.
notes: Not WordPress (custom CMS). No /feed or wp-json; /sitemap.xml 404s. Publications and testimony are separate listings, each paginated by item offset in the path (/publications/P8, /news/c/testimony/P20), 8 per page for publications and 20 per page for testimony; last page is /publications/P264 (about 272 items total). RSS exists at /news/rss (about 254 KB) but covers news items, not the publications listing. Titles use curly apostrophes; dates render as 'Jun. 2026' on publications and 'July 8th, 2026' on testimony.

name: Federation of Protestant Welfare Agencies
recommendations_evidence: "FPWA Testimony: New York City Council Committee on General Welfare FY27 Preliminary Budget Hearing" (March 20, 2026), alongside "True Cost of Economic Security Policy Implications for New York City" (October 10, 2025).

volume_2025_plus.note: 6 dated items on /resource-center/reports-briefs/ since 2025-01-01 (Mar 11 2026; Dec 18 2025 x2; Oct 10 2025; Aug 26 2025; Jan 23 2025 - page 2 starts at Dec 2023) plus 17 dated items on /resource-center/testimony/ (all 10 on page 1 back to Sep 23 2025, plus 7 on page 2 back to Feb 18 2025).

verdict_reason: Publishes dated research reports and a steady stream of New York City Council budget and oversight testimony with explicit recommendations to city government.
notes: WordPress but the REST API is locked: /wp-json/wp/v2/types returns 401 {"code":"rest_cannot_access","message":"DRA: Only authenticated users can access the REST API."}. /feed redirects to the homepage. HTML scraping works fine with a browser UA. Resource Center is split into sub-listings (reports-briefs, testimony, blogs, in-the-news); reports-briefs has 2 pages and testimony has 4, paginated as /page/2/. Pages are heavy (about 370-380 KB each) and carry a GDPR cookie banner in markup. The combined listing at /resource-center/ runs 32 pages.

name: Human Services Council of New York
recommendations_evidence: "Essential or Expendable? How Human Services Supported Communities Through COVID-19 and Recommendations to Support an Equitable Recovery" - the taskforce "developed recommendations for steps the City and State can take to support a resilient and strong sector"; most recent is "The Impact of NYC's For-Profit Migrant Contracts" (report PDF dated December 2025).

volume_2025_plus.note: The /reports/ listing shows no dates at all. Only one of its 17 entries falls in the window: 'The Impact of NYC's For-Profit Migrant Contracts', whose cover image is at /wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ and whose PDF is a Squarespace asset with epoch 1765207398678 = December 8, 2025. Every other report links to a PDF under /uploads/ dated 2021 or earlier, or to the pre-2017 /uploads/Initiatives|Reports/ tree. The 7 wp-json posts since 2025-01-01 are all press clips about HSC, not HSC publications, and a wp-json search for 'testimony' returns one item from 2019.

verdict_reason: The reports are genuine policy documents with explicit recommendations to New York City government, but only one has appeared since 2025-01-01 and the listing carries no dates, so the ingestible volume is close to nil.
notes: WordPress; wp-json/wp/v2 open. The 'news' category (324 posts) is a media-clip archive of coverage about HSC, not HSC's own output, so the RSS feed is misleading as a publications feed. /reports/ is a static hand-built page with no dates and no pagination; report PDFs live variously on the site and on Squarespace. /advocacy/ is a near-empty page holding a single 2020 news clip. The #JustPay campaign lives on a separate Squarespace site at justpayny.org whose Facts & Research page cites outside research (New School, IBO, FPI), not new HSC publications.

name: Institute for Children, Poverty and Homelessness
recommendations_evidence: "THE HIDDEN HOMELESS: What NYC Candidates Should Know About Family Homelessness: May 8, 2025 Edition" states "Sufficient funding should be allocated toward shelter-based services such as job training for parents" and that "City officials need to be ready to support efforts that improve the educational outcomes for homeless students."

volume_2025_plus.note: X-WP-Total: 8 from https://www.icph.org/wp-json/wp/v2/icph_reports?after=2025-01-01T00:00:00, cross-checked against the dates printed on the /reports listing page: 2026-06-03, 2026-04-30, 2025-11-24, 2025-09-25, 2025-08-21, 2025-06-30, 2025-05-27, 2025-05-08. The icph_uncensored, icph_resources and icph_infographic custom post types all return X-WP-Total: 0 for the same window, so they add nothing.

verdict_reason: A research institute whose New York City family-homelessness reports carry explicit funding and service recommendations aimed at city officials, even though some items are purely descriptive.
notes: icphusa.org redirects to icph.org, which redirects to www.icph.org - use the www host or REST links come back inconsistent. wp-json/wp/v2/types exposes ten custom post types; reports live in icph_reports (80 items, 2 REST pages at per_page=50). The HTML /reports page is server-rendered with visible dates and paginates 1..7. Output is uneven: 'Federal SNAP Changes Threaten Stability for NYC Families in Shelter' (Nov 24, 2025) is descriptive and makes no city recommendation, while the Hidden Homeless candidate fact sheets do. Roughly half the recent catalogue is national, New Jersey or rural rather than New York City, hence nyc_focus 'partial'.

name: New York Immigration Coalition
recommendations_evidence: Press release, June 10, 2026: "Advocates called on NYC Council and the Mamdani administration to meet this moment with bold action by allocating $188M for immigration legal services, passing the NYC Know Your Rights Act (Intro 55)..." - but this is a rally press release, not a report or testimony.

volume_2025_plus.note: x-wp-total on /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?after=2025-01-01 is 185; 184 of those sit in the Press Releases category (x-wp-total for categories=16 with the same after filter). Zero reports and zero testimony in the window: the Reports category (id 18) holds 7 posts, newest June 20, 2017, and a wp-json search for 'testimony' returns nothing newer than 2019.

verdict_reason: Since 2025 the published output is effectively all press releases - the last posted report is 2017 and the last posted testimony is 2019 - so it meets the bar's exclusion for a pure press-release operation despite making explicit budget asks of city government.
notes: WordPress; wp-json/wp/v2 open and reliable (types, categories, posts, search all 200). Only custom post type is 'partner'. The /news-at-the-nyic/press-releases/ page is a very large single-page archive (about 968 KB) with roughly 500 permalinks in the source, including 67 dated 2026 and 117 dated 2025, but the item titles/dates are injected by JavaScript so plain HTML parsing yields links only. Scope is New York City plus Long Island and statewide, hence partial NYC focus.

name: New Yorkers for Parks
recommendations_evidence: "Play Fair Coalition First 100 Days for Parks Agenda" (PDF Last-Modified 2025-01-07) and "Building the Future of New York: Parks and Open Space", described on the site as "Recommendations for NYC's recovery by NY4P and the New York Building Congress".

volume_2025_plus.note: The research library's 2025 year filter (https://ny4p.org/data-and-research/research-library/2025) returns 5 'Open Space Solutions 2025' community-district reports (Queens CB2, Brooklyn CB17, Brooklyn CB11, Bronx CB5, Manhattan CB10). Add the Play Fair First 100 Days for Parks Agenda PDF, whose server Last-Modified header is 2025-01-07, for 6. There is no 2026 option in the year filter, so nothing has been added to the library this year.

verdict_reason: A real, dated research library of open-space analyses and budget agendas addressed to the Parks Department, City Council and mayor, though the output is bursty rather than continuous.
notes: Custom CMS - no feed at all (/feed and /rss.xml both return the 'Page Not Found - NY4P' template). The library front page renders items into a map widget, but the year-filtered URLs (/research-library/2025 etc.) are server-rendered and scrapeable. Many items are PDF-only under /client-uploads/pdf/ with no on-page date; the PDF HTTP Last-Modified header is the most reliable date signal. Play Fair budget statements also appear under /news.

name: Nonprofit New York
recommendations_evidence: Page headed "Nonprofit new york 2024 policy platform": "City Contracting Reform. Nonprofit New York supports the following legislation to improve city contracting for nonprofit organizations: Int 0510 (Stevens) would establish prevailing wage requirements for city-contracted human service workers."

volume_2025_plus.note: x-wp-total on /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?after=2025-01-01 is 2, and both are organizational announcements: 'Nonprofit New York Launches Group Retirement Plan for Member Organizations' (2026-04-02) and 'Jacqueline M. Ebanks Named Permanent President & CEO' (2025-08-04). The advocacy-policy category (id 87, 120 posts) has nothing newer than 2024-07-08, and its items are budget statements and campaign updates rather than reports. Zero papers, reports or testimony in the window.

verdict_reason: Output is membership services, trainings and campaign statements - the policy platform is an undated static page last revised for 2024, and nothing resembling a report or testimony has been published since 2025-01-01.
notes: WordPress with Elementor; wp-json/wp/v2 open, custom types include members-hub, team-bio, training-and-event. Pages are very large (600-800 KB) because of Elementor markup. The policy platform lives at /policy-platform/ as a single undated page; there is no dated reports or testimony listing anywhere on the site. The monthly Policy Roundup referenced on /advocacy/ is a member communication, not a public listing.

name: Open Plans
recommendations_evidence: "Hit the Brakes: Understanding and reducing vehicle miles traveled in NYC" (October 2025), whose blurb says it "urges NYC to set a citywide goal to reduce driving, invest in tools for measuring VMT, reconsider policies that increase driving, and adopt proven strategies that reduce optional driving."

volume_2025_plus.note: Counted month-dated entries on https://www.openplans.org/reports on or after January 2025: July 2026 (robotaxis/AVs), January 2026 (School Streets), October 2025 (VMT), September 2025 (curb management), March 2025 (outdoor dining). The site also lists a '2026 Agenda for a Livable City' and 'Livability Priorities for Mayor Mamdani' under Resources, which are undated on the nav and not counted here.

verdict_reason: Small but high-signal: every report is a New York City policy evaluation with named recommendations to DOT and City Hall, and each carries a publication month.
notes: Squarespace; /reports is a static page so /reports?format=rss returns HTTP 400. A collection feed exists at /blog?format=rss but carries commentary. Dates are month-level only (no day). Also runs Streetsblog NYC and Streetfilms as sister organizations - those are news outlets and should not be folded in.

name: Riders Alliance
recommendations_evidence: Reports page carries "2022 Riders Agenda for New York" calling on the governor to "stop the fare hike, deliver 6-minute subway and bus service, double accessibility, and implement congestion pricing" - but nothing on that page is dated after 2022.

volume_2025_plus.note: The reports-resources page lists no item newer than 2022. The /news RSS feed returned 15 items back to December 2024; every 2025 and 2026 item read as a campaign update, endorsement or budget-win announcement (e.g. 2026-06-30 'Riders bank a major win for affordable transit', 2025-05-06 'Riders Alliance Endorses Zohran Mamdani for Mayor!'), not a report or testimony.

verdict_reason: Recent output is campaign organizing and press posts; the reports page has been dormant since 2022, so there is no current publication stream to ingest.
notes: ridersny.org redirects to ridersalliance.org. Squarespace: /news?format=rss works, /reports-resources?format=rss returns HTTP 400. Worth re-checking in a year if they restart the reports program.

name: Robin Hood Foundation
recommendations_evidence: "Partnership Against Poverty: An Agenda for Collaboration with the Mamdani Administration" (December 2025) states "The incoming administration must scale these successes with urgency" across five priority areas; separately "NYC Needs Additional Funds to Maintain Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP) Vouchers" (March 2025).

volume_2025_plus.note: Parsed the 107 unique /reports/ links on https://robinhood.org/research/, whose anchor text carries a 'Month Year' prefix. 24 are dated 2025-01 or later (15 Poverty Tracker items, 9 funded policy-research items). Two more listed links carry no date in the anchor text and were dated by opening them: 'Partnership Against Poverty: An Agenda for Collaboration with the Mamdani Administration' (December 2025, per the surrounding listing text) and 'Spotlight on: Rent Stabilization in New York City' (datePublished 2026-06-22 in the page JSON-LD). 24 + 2 = 26.

verdict_reason: Poverty Tracker reports themselves are descriptive measurement, but Robin Hood's Policy Research line and its mayoral-agenda documents make explicit, itemized recommendations to New York City government.
notes: Poverty Tracker finding, per the task question: the Poverty Tracker series (with the Columbia University Center on Poverty and Social Policy) is predominantly DESCRIPTIVE measurement - the July 2025 Housing Affordability spotlight, for example, quantifies that 50,000 more New Yorkers would fall below the poverty line if federal housing assistance were cut but issues no affirmative city ask. The prescriptive material sits in the separate 'Policy Research' block on the same page (externally authored, Robin-Hood-funded studies from Columbia, Urban Institute, CSS, Brookings, Baruch/CUNY, NYU Furman) and in the Partnership Against Poverty mayoral agenda. Fetch gotchas: /feed/ is 1,382 bytes and wp/v2/posts returns []; wp-json/wp/v2/types lists custom types (news, events, issue, immersive-articles, executive-summary, grantees) but reports are NOT among them - there is no REST collection for /reports/. /poverty-tracker/ redirects to /research/. The /research/ page is fully server-rendered with all 107 reports on one page and no pagination; dates must be parsed from the anchor text prefix, and the two featured items at the top of each block have promotional anchor text ('Read the report') instead of a date.

name: The Trust for Governors Island
recommendations_evidence: None found. Its published documents are the operating and disclosure filings a public authority must post, plus master-plan and public-season presentations - not recommendations addressed to city government.

volume_2025_plus.note: Unverifiable from here. govisland.org returned HTTP 000 (connection reset) to curl and ECONNRESET to WebFetch across repeated attempts; the live domain appears to be govisland.com. No publications listing could be fetched and confirmed, so no count is asserted.

verdict_reason: It is a nonprofit corporation created by the City of New York to operate the island - a government instrumentality subject to Public Authorities Accountability Act posting requirements, not an outside voice making recommendations to city government.
notes: Included only to record the negative finding, since it was named as a candidate. Correct domain is govisland.com; govisland.org was unreachable during this check. If revisited, verify against https://www.govisland.com/about/planning-and-governance rather than assuming.

name: Transportation Alternatives
recommendations_evidence: "The Road to Affordability: A Streets and Transportation Agenda for the Next Mayor of NYC" (November 13, 2025); the page says the reports "hold New York City decision-makers to the highest standard of efficacy."

volume_2025_plus.note: Counted dated entries on https://transalt.org/reports with dates on or after 2025-01-01: 2026-07-13, 2026-03-17, 2025-11-13, 2025-10-07, 2025-06-05, 2025-05-15, 2025-04-16.

verdict_reason: A sustained original-research program whose reports make explicit, addressable proposals to New York City agencies and elected officials.
notes: Squarespace site, but /reports is a static page, not a collection: /reports?format=rss returns HTTP 400 'Unknown response format for page type'. Collection feeds exist only for /blog and /press-releases, which carry commentary and press rather than reports. Scrape the /reports page; items before 2018 are listed under 'Older Reports' with parenthetical month-year rather than a date field.

name: Tri-State Transportation Campaign
recommendations_evidence: "Riders' Recommendations for the Post-COVID Commute" (2020-06-10) and "Bidding for a Better Bee-Line: Bringing Westchester's Bus System into the Future" (2022-10-31) - both older than the 2025 cutoff.

volume_2025_plus.note: The publication archive is a Document Library Pro custom post type. Pulling https://tstc.org/wp-json/wp/v2/dlp_document?per_page=50&orderby=date&order=desc returned 50 records whose newest is 2024-07-08 ('The Buzz on the Bee-Line 2.0'). Nothing dated 2025 or later.

verdict_reason: The publication archive has produced nothing since mid-2024, and its scope is the New York, New Jersey and Connecticut region rather than New York City government specifically.
notes: The /resources/ page renders 'Loading publications...' and fills in via JavaScript, but the underlying REST endpoint wp-json/wp/v2/dlp_document is open and clean, so no browser is needed if this is ever revisited.

name: United Neighborhood Houses
recommendations_evidence: Policy brief "A NORC in Every Neighborhood: Expanding Naturally Occurring Retirement Communities to Meet the Needs of Older New Yorkers" - "UNH urges the City to invest $10 million in the FY27 budget to ensure that there is a NORC in every neighborhood."

volume_2025_plus.note: 40 dated testimony items on /testimonies with a date on or after 2025-01-01 (from 'May 1, 2026' down to 'February 12, 2025'; the next item is October 30, 2024). Counted from the 72 date lines on the single un-paginated listing page. Reports and briefs are additional but carry no publication dates on /reports or /briefs, so they are not included in this count.

verdict_reason: Publishes a dense, dated stream of New York City Council testimony plus reports and briefs that name specific dollar amounts and program changes for city government.
notes: NationBuilder, not WordPress - the earlier 403 on wp-json was a Cloudflare challenge on a path that does not exist as an API here (the interstitial 'Just a moment...' page still returns for /wp-json/*). /feed/ 404s. Homepage and all listing pages fetch cleanly with a browser UA via curl. /testimonies is a single un-paginated page listing every testimony back to January 2023, each with a 'Download the testimony' link to a PDF - full text is PDF-only. /reports and /briefs have descriptive blurbs and PDF links but no dates. /publications is just a hub with no items.

name: United Way of New York City
recommendations_evidence: "NYC Cost of Living Policy Recommendations" (April 10, 2024): "Our policy brief uses findings from the report to recommend specific strategies and policies for local, state, and federal governments that will increase incomes and reduce expenses so all New Yorkers can thrive."

volume_2025_plus.note: x-wp-total on /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?after=2025-01-01 is 327, but the categories show what those are: 'snippets' (288) is a media-clip archive and most posts are double-filed as snippets plus news, covering the Gridiron Gala, grant announcements and press statements. The advocacy category (id 60) has 14 items since 2025-01-01, all statements, joint statements, convenings and events. No report or policy brief in the window: the True Cost of Living page is stamped 'Copyright (c) 2024' and its policy brief dates to March 2024.

verdict_reason: Since 2025 the output is program news, press statements and media clips; its one genuine policy-brief line (True Cost of Living, with Fund for the City of New York) has published nothing new since March 2024.
notes: WordPress with Divi; wp-json/wp/v2 open, custom types project/honoree/dnxte_popup. www redirects to the apex domain. Nearly every post is duplicated across the 'snippets' and 'news'/'blog' categories, so raw post counts roughly double the real item count. The site carries many stale draft pages (test page2, Home Beta 1023 V1, etc.) that surface in wp-json search. The True Cost of Living research is co-published with Fund for the City of New York and the underlying methodology PDF is hosted on fpwa.org.

name: Waterfront Alliance
recommendations_evidence: "Waterfront Alliance Testimony for New York City Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE) Hearing RE: Streamlining Waterfront Permitting" (July 13, 2026); also "Embracing the Waterfront: First 100 Day Priorities for the Next Mayoral Administration of New York City".

volume_2025_plus.note: Counted dated entries in the Public Testimony and Statements archive: 23 items dated in 2025 and 10 in 2026 through July 13. Cross-checked against PDF links under /wp-content/uploads/, which give the same 2025=23, 2026=10 split. Roughly half are addressed to New York City bodies (City Council committees, DOB, HPD, COGE); the rest go to state, New Jersey or federal agencies. Policy platforms and fact sheets on the parent page are additional.

verdict_reason: One of the most consistent producers of dated New York City Council testimony and city agency rule comments in the set, with an archive already structured by date.
notes: WordPress, but the wp-json types endpoint returns an error object and the category feed at .../public-testimony-statements/feed/ is valid RSS with zero <item> elements, so the custom 'policy document' post type is not exposed. Scrape the HTML archive: it is a year-accordion where each date heading can carry more than one document, and items link straight to PDFs. Needs a New York City filter - the archive mixes NYC, New York State, New Jersey and federal advocacy.

name: Win (Women In Need)
recommendations_evidence: "THE COST OF INACTION: How Fully Implementing CityFHEPS Expansion Reforms Could Have Saved New York City..." (June 04, 2026), alongside "NYC Housing Sector Calls for CityFHEPS Expansion" (June 01, 2026), which opens "Dear Mayor Mamdani."

volume_2025_plus.note: Counted every dated PDF item across all 9 pages of the paginated policy listing (52 dated items total) and kept those dated 2025-01-01 or later: 6 in 2026 (Jan 29, Feb 12, Mar 04, Apr 15, Jun 01, Jun 04) and 8 in 2025 (Jan 07, Apr 17 x2, Jun 14, Sep 12, Oct 15, Dec 03, Dec 16). Dates are printed on the listing page next to each item.

verdict_reason: A shelter provider that also publishes dated policy reports and briefs addressed directly to the mayor and city agencies with specific budget and CityFHEPS asks.
notes: Paginated at /policy-and-advocacy/page/N/ through page 9; page 10 and beyond return HTTP 200 with no items rather than 404, so stop on an empty item count, not on status. Every item is a PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ with the date rendered in the anchor text (e.g. 'Win | June 04, 2026'), so the anchor text must be parsed for the date. www.winnyc.org 404s on some paths and redirects to the apex host - use https://winnyc.org. wp-json/wp/v2/types exposes no custom post types and the only category is 'uncategorized', so /feed/ and the REST posts endpoint mix press items with policy items and cannot be used to isolate reports.
